law: What a Code is called once it's shared by more than one person. D&D class: — a reputation concept, not a Law.
A curved cousin of Blade, favoring the draw strike over the shape itself. D&D class: Fighter, Samurai.

Sadness is its own entity, formed when Dark was siphoned down to grief alone, leaving every other negative feeling behind in the process. D&D class: Cleric, Grave Domain (official subclass, reflavored to grief itself rather than death in general).
A detection Law, weaker than Identify since it only confirms something's there, not what it actually is. D&D class: Wizard, School of Divination.
What's left once Regeneration or Heal finishes closing something that Decay or a blade opened. D&D class: — a resulting mark, not a class.
The refined sense cousin of Smell, strong enough to track rather than just notice. D&D class: — a trained sense, not a class.
A splinter of Dark, colder and more deliberate than Anger. D&D class: Warlock, The Hexblade.
A shape more Man Made than magical, occasionally paired with Turn for anything that needs binding rather than striking. D&D class: Artificer, Battle Smith.
A curved cousin of Blade, shaped more for Blacksmith's harvest tools than Battle Axe's battlefield ones, though it's ended up in both. D&D class: Fighter, Rune Knight.
What separates an Entity from a tool, regardless of whether it started as either one. D&D class: — a definitional threshold, not a class.
The paired opposite of Fusion, pulling two combined things back apart, though rarely as cleanly as they were joined. D&D class: Wizard, School of Conjuration.
The stillest splinter of Light, holding neither the reach of Hope nor the heat of Love. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Open Hand.

The paired opposite of Sovereignty, and the more common condition among anyone without Royalty behind them. D&D class: — the concept underlying the Warlock class generally (a pact is servitude to a patron), not a subclass of its own.
Cast by Dark but not made of it, closer to an absence of Light than a Law of its own. D&D class: Sorcerer, Shadow Magic.
Condensed from the Shade a corpse leaves behind rather than the corpse itself, with no physical form to speak of — weak in a straight fight, but nearly impossible to hit.

Shaman isn't a Law or a Class in its own right — it's a description of a bloodline, the same way Elves is. Those born into it sit closer to the Spirit Realm than an ordinary mortal, and draw more readily on whatever's left of a progenitor spirit when they acquire a Class tied to one. In practice thi
A rarer summon, holding onto roughly a quarter of the original's power along with a borrowed cousin of Transformation, letting it wear the shape of anything else it's absorbed.
The defensive twin to Blade, drawn from the same Iron and Steel but shaped to stop rather than to cut. D&D class: Barbarian, Path of the Totem Warrior.
A short, sharp release Law, related to Electric more often than not but not bound to it. D&D class: Sorcerer, Storm Sorcery.
The paired opposite of Longer, and the more common choice for anything meant to be concealed. D&D class: — a size modifier, not a class.
A narrow Transmission, meant to be noticed rather than understood. D&D class: — too narrow for its own class.

Singularity is the entity formed when a piece of Cosmic was siphoned off and collapsed entirely inward, the most extreme of the four, too unstable for anyone but the strongest to hold onto for long. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Astral Self (official subclass).
A slower, quieter version of Theft, pulling power away without the target noticing until it's already gone. D&D class: Rogue, Arcane Trickster.

Skeleton are considered the worst of the summon as it can be made from any corpse taking around 1/20 of the original being power being unable to do anything magical or use any skill only being physical.
A small Void law that lets a moment or a step be passed over entirely, never used carelessly near Causality. D&D class: Rogue, Scout.
The part of Bones most often kept as proof of a kill or a summon, whether or not it still holds any power. D&D class: — a trophy item, not a class.
Another of the Original Sin cluster, closer to Depression than to Fatigue since it dulls the will rather than the body. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Long Death.
The paired opposite of Speed, and the more commonly weaponized of the two. D&D class: Ranger, Gloom Stalker.
The paired opposite of Bigger, and the safer of the two to test on something living. D&D class: — a size modifier, not a class.
The least refined of the five senses, useful mostly to those who hunt rather than those who fight. D&D class: — a trained sense, not a class of its own.
Paired opposite of Always, a modifier for a Law that only works under conditions still being worked out. D&D class: — a modifier, not a class.
Anything that bends where a thing is rather than when it is, which is why it's rarely paired with Time Laws. D&D class: Warlock, The Great Old One.
A cousin of Blade stretched long, closer to Dart in how it's used than to Axe in how it's shaped. D&D class: Fighter, Purple Dragon Knight.
Bodiless like a Wraith but bound by unfinished business instead of a necromancer's ritual, which is why it can't be commanded nearly as reliably.
The raw ability a Verbal caster draws on, distinct from any single Word itself. D&D class: Bard, College of Eloquence.
A power coming from the Void, being one of the more abstract law allowing one to add rotation to any object. D&D class: Sorcerer, Wild Magic (official subclass).

progTitle: the Nameless Shade of Spirit (Martial Spirit)
law: The internal reserve a Martial cultivator builds up over years, separate from anything pulled from the Spirit Realm despite the name. D&D class: — the resource underlying the Monk class's Ki generally, not a subclass of its own.
A shape Law that turns one strike into two, more often paired with Dagger than with anything heavier. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Kensei.
The Law reached for once something else — a Fusion, a Curse, a Pacts deal — starts coming apart on its own. D&D class: Paladin, Oath of Redemption.

Star is the entity formed when a piece of Cosmic was siphoned off and condensed inward instead, packed so tightly it started to burn on its own. D&D class: Cleric, Light Domain (official subclass, reflavored to raw starlight rather than a god's radiance).
A distant cousin of Plasma, carrying the same Cosmic essence but faint enough for mortals to actually touch. D&D class: Cleric, Light Domain.
The paired opposite of Signal, noise where a message was supposed to be. D&D class: — too narrow for its own class.
The power being the evolved version of Iron, made after Iron was locked in the spirit realm, D&D class: Artificer, Armorer.
A splinter closer to Fear and Fatigue both, the body's answer to the Mortal Realm's pressure rather than the mind's. D&D class: Barbarian, Path of the Zealot.
The opposite of Add, a Void law of plain decrease rather than Destruction's violence. D&D class: — a math modifier, not a class.

Sylph is the spirit of Air, one of the progenitors who lived in the Spirit Realm before her corpse became the Air Law. The old records call her the only progenitor that never stayed in one place long enough to be drawn: a voice, a pressure, a direction the grass bent. Sylph left more children than a
A Nature Law binding two Lives together for mutual benefit, gentler than anything Pacts would ask for. D&D class: Ranger, Beast Master.
A Void law of balance in shape rather than in Balance itself, opposed by Asymmetry. D&D class: Artificer, Armorer.
The paired opposite of Gift, and the more common of the two by far. D&D class: Rogue, Thief.
The Law behind binding an Animal or Beastman to a will other than its own, without going as far as Imprison. D&D class: Ranger, Beast Master.
One of the five senses a Martial cultivator learns to refine past its ordinary mortal limit. D&D class: — a trained sense, not a class of its own.
What Man Made things are called when they work without needing any Law at all. D&D class: — the concept underlying the Artificer class generally, not a subclass of its own.
A Mental Law that skips Speech and Word entirely, reaching mind to mind instead. D&D class: Sorcerer, Aberrant Mind.
The rhythm a Martial cultivator or a Music caster keeps, more felt than counted. D&D class: — a felt quality, not a class.

The Law of reshaping land at scale: raising hills, draining swamps, turning desert to field. Where Earth moves stone and Gnome's remains let the wielder pass through it, Terraformation changes what a place is . It sits between Natural and Man Made: the result looks natural, but something decided it.
A cousin of Take, specifically aimed at stealing a Law itself rather than an object. D&D class: Rogue, Thief.
The paired opposite of Wider, favored for anything meant to slip through a gap. D&D class: — a size modifier, not a class.

Time is its own entity, formed when the Void was siphoned in on itself and folded until it produced something capable of measuring its own passing, rather than simply being another abstract law sitting beside it. D&D class: Wizard, Chronurgy Magic (official subclass).

progTitle: the Hidden Shade of Time Duration
law: A narrower cousin of Time itself, measuring only how long something lasts rather than bending its pace. D&D class: Wizard, Chronurgy Magic.
The sense Martial cultivators refine last, since numbing it is often more useful in a fight than sharpening it. D&D class: — a trained sense, not a class of its own.
What Culture becomes once it's held onto past the point anyone remembers why. D&D class: Bard, College of Lore.
The deliberate, repeated practice behind both Learning and Aptitude, though it can't create the second on its own. D&D class: — a meta process, not a class.
A cousin of Telepathy, sending a Law's effect rather than a thought. D&D class: Sorcerer, Aberrant Mind.
The heart of Alchemy, turning one substance into another rather than merely shaping it. D&D class: Wizard, School of Transmutation.
The Law behind any contest meant to settle something — a duel, a War, a Battle — rather than the fighting itself. D&D class: Paladin, Oath of the Crown.
A splinter of Light laid between two people rather than felt alone, undone entirely by Betrayal. D&D class: Paladin, Oath of the Crown.
A shape adjacent Law, rotating something in place rather than moving it, distinct from Spin's more violent version of the same idea. D&D class: Wizard, Bladesinging.
A sharper, more forceful cousin of Turn, often used to break rather than simply reposition. D&D class: Barbarian, Path of the Berserker.
A Law that only works in situations where the outcome genuinely isn't decided yet — useless in anything already certain, including most fights. D&D class: Sorcerer, Wild Magic.

progTitle: the Shrouded Shade of Undead Summoning
law: Undead summoning types, roughly ordered from weakest to strongest by how much of the original's power a corpse can hold onto. A fresher, more intact, or more deliberately preserved corpse always keeps more than a bare skeleton does — and the strongest two on this list, Lich and Grim Reaper, aren't c

Undine is the spirit of Water, one of the progenitors dwelling in the Spirit Realm before its corpse became the Water Law. Depicted in what little survives of the old records as formless and restless — never the same shape twice, always moving even when nothing around it did. Undine's death produced
The honest answer for whatever hasn't been placed on this list yet — including, for now, whatever The Beyond actually is. D&D class: — a placeholder concept, not a class.
The paired opposite of Weave, undoing a combined spell back into its separate pieces. D&D class: Wizard, School of Abjuration.
One of the Undead Summoning types, feeding on Blood rather than simply existing off of borrowed Life.
The practice of casting through Speech instead of gesture or rune, faster but impossible to use in silence. D&D class: — the concept underlying the Bard class generally, not a subclass of its own.

Created when Sylph used the power of Spin creating a mix between the two neither stronger nor weaker that both creating 4 of Sylph only children being Boreas, Zephyrus, Notus, Eurus. D&D class: Warlock, patron being Vortex itself — an unstable, fused entity rather than a single god.
A defensive shape, wider than Line and meant to stop rather than travel. D&D class: Wizard, School of Abjuration.
Land left to rot the way Swamp is Mud left to rot, claimed partly by Decay. D&D class: Druid, Circle of Spores.

Starts as weak as a Ghoul but doesn't stay that way, growing stronger the more Life it consumes from the living rather than simply holding onto what the corpse had left, tied loosely to the same hunger behind Famine.
Paired opposite of Dry, tied more to Water in passing than in any direct descent. D&D class: — a state modifier, not a class.
Paired with Black more by convention than by any real connection to Light or Dark. D&D class: — a descriptive pairing, not a Law with its own class.
Paired opposite of Thinner, applied to a shape's spread rather than its length. D&D class: — a size modifier, not a class.

The rarest and least reliable Law on record, said to answer to no realm at all — not Divine, not the Void, not even Infinatas. D&D class: — reserved; this is the Wish spell itself, the ceiling of what any full caster can ever reach, not tied to one class or subclass.
Bigger than Nature — the whole physical shape of the Mortal Realm, not just what grows or erodes in it. D&D class: — too vast/foundational for a single class.

The mortal act that keeps a god's power from thinning the way Light and Dark already have. D&D class: — the mechanic underlying the Cleric class generally, not a subclass of its own. See God Contracts for the ranked contracts gods offer mortals.

Has no Corpse at all, summoned instead from a fragment of Spirit left over after death, weaker in body than almost anything on this list but the first to hold onto a sliver of the original's magic instead of none.
The other half of Yin, and just as reliant on its opposite to mean anything. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Sun Soul.
Half of a pairing with Yang, tied loosely to Balance though neither half works as well alone. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Open Hand.

Zephyrus being a soft giant bring forth Summer, known to be coping with his mother death with pure joy, she is known to be worse that Boreas when her mother the being Sylph, is mention killing those who say it with pure heat. She is one of the many deity behind the Season
The Void's law of nothing, quieter than Emptiness since it describes an absence of number rather than an absence of space. D&D class: Fighter, Eldritch Knight.
Needs a corpse with its Flesh still mostly intact, keeping slightly more power than a Skeleton and just enough crude muscle memory to move the way it used to, though never with any skill behind it.
A title earned through Battle and Loyalty together, rarely through either alone. D&D class: Paladin, Oath of the Crown.
